mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with tightened financial conditions that reduce equity discounting, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the identified Fed rate hike episode, with p-value > 0.05 in a two-tailed test against baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 5% for two consecutive months predicts a decline in consumer and business confidence, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: High unemployment or weak wage growth
failure_condition: 20-day and 60-day forward returns are both positive, or UNRATE decline is not statistically significant (p > 0.1) in a regression controlling for inflation and GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real private consumption) exceeds INDPRO by more than 10% for three consecutive months, it indicates strong consumer demand that supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a regression with controls for inflation and interest rates.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 8% in a month coincides with supply-side shocks that depress corporate earnings expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >= 8% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or indistinguishable from baseline (p > 0.1) during comparable supply shocks.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) rises by more than 1% in a month while FEDFUNDS remains below 2%, it signals unexpected inflation pressure without policy tightening, which tends to depress equity valuations and produce negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >1% and FEDFUNDS < 2% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or the interaction term is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS (employment) by over 50,000 in a month suggests labor market strength that can support economic momentum and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >50,000 in a single month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or not statistically significant (p > 0.1) in a regression with lagged GDP and inflation.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of RSAFS (retail sales) above 3% of the prior month's level indicate accelerating consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS grows by >3% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period (three months) of declining HOUST (housing starts) below INDPRO suggests a supply glut, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < INDPRO for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05).
